scenes.title: 1974 Queen Square Perimeter Arc: Patient D.B. Fixing Straight Ahead While Pointing Dead-Center Into His 'Blind' Left Field

layout.description: Sunlit 1974 British hospital neuro-ophthalmology testing room featuring a curved white semicircular perimeter screen with a central fixation cross; on the right ('Intact Field') and left ('Consciously Blind Left Field') sit silent optical projection spots and 'X vs O' plaques, alongside a scorecard reading 'Conscious Sight: 0% | Forced-Choice Pointing: 92%'.

positions.who: Patient D.B. (mannequin in 1974 knit V-neck jumper over collared shirt)
positions.where: chin resting steadily on the white perimeter chin-rest, eyes locked strictly on the center cross, extending his index finger to touch the silent light spot in his 'blind' left arc while shaking his head saying he saw nothing

positions.who: Lawrence Weiskrantz & Elizabeth Warrington (mannequins in 1974 white clinical coats)
positions.where: silently projecting a silent target and 'X / O' grating into the left arc, then turning the 92%-accurate scorecard around to show the astonished patient

props.name: curved white clinical perimeter arc with central fixation cross
props.period_detail: separates D.B.'s intact right field from his V1-lesioned blind left field

props.name: silent light-spot projector & 'X vs O' orientation paddles
props.period_detail: zero sound cues — pure silent visual targets inside the blind hemifield
props.physical_behavior: tests location pointing AND shape orientation

props.name: 'Seen: 0 / 30 — Pointed Accurately: 28 / 30 (93%)' reveal clipboard
props.period_detail: captures D.B.'s own famous disbelief when shown his hit map
props.physical_behavior: delivers the core human astonishment beat

actions.verb_sequence: flashes a silent target spot 20 degrees inside D.B.'s blind left arc and prompts 'Just guess with your finger' -> Patient D.B. reaches smoothly and touches dead-center on the spot while reporting 'Nothing there'
turns the cluster-dotted target map around -> Patient D.B. leans back in amazement seeing 28 bullseyes

reactions.reaction: stares wide-eyed at his own bullseye target sheet ('I swear it was pure guesswork!')
record the birth of 'Blindsight' for Brain and The Lancet

scenes.wardrobe: 1974 British clinical coats over tweed/blouse; patient V-neck wool jumper and collared shirt.
scenes.recognition_hook: He swears on his life the left half of the screen is empty — then puts his finger bullseye on 28 out of 30 silent targets.

key_visual.description: a 1974 clinical testing room where a seated patient on a chin-rest stares straight ahead while pointing accurately at a silent target on the left half of a curved white perimeter screen beside a 93% accuracy clipboard

scenes.title: 2008 Corridor Obstacle Course Without V1 (Patient T.N.)

layout.description: Bright sunlit hospital corridor scattered with low wooden chairs, cardboard boxes, and paper-roll obstacles.

positions.where: walking unassisted down the bright corridor side-stepping every chair and box cleanly without a cane or collision
trailing safely a step behind with dropped jaws and clipboards

props.name: staggered hallway chairs & boxes
props.period_detail: navigated with zero collisions despite bilateral V1 loss
props.physical_behavior: de Gelder et al. 2008 landmark video proof

actions.verb_sequence: weaves left around a chair and steps smoothly past a box while reporting zero conscious sight

reactions.reaction: applaud quietly at intact subcortical dorsal navigation

scenes.recognition_hook: Zero primary visual cortex in either hemisphere — yet his ancient midbrain radar steers his feet cleanly around every chair in the hall.

scenes.title: Affective Blindsight: Catching Fear Without Seeing a Face

layout.description: Clean testing booth flashing a fearful vs smiling mannequin portrait into the blind field while tiny cheek sensors record involuntary mimicry.

positions.where: reporting an empty screen while their brow subtly knits on unseen fear cards and relaxes on unseen smile cards

props.name: facial expression cards & amygdala-colliculus pathway diagram
props.period_detail: proves unseen emotions reach amygdala via superior colliculus

actions.verb_sequence: flashes unseen smile card -> participant's zygomatic cheek trace lifts automatically

scenes.wardrobe: Clean modern shirt and lab coat.
scenes.recognition_hook: Even when conscious sight is pitch-dark, an unseen smile or frightened face reaches your amygdala and moves your own cheek muscles.

scenes.title: Why You Still Need Consciousness: The Untouched Glass of Water

layout.description: Sunlit table where a clear glass of water sits in the blind left field — untouched until someone prompts a guess.

positions.where: feeling thirsty yet never spontaneously reaching left until turning head to bring the glass into conscious sight

props.name: clear water glass on left vs right side of table
props.period_detail: illustrates what unconscious blindsight CANNOT do: initiate spontaneous self-chosen goals

actions.verb_sequence: ignores glass in blind zone -> turns eyes into intact conscious field -> smiles and picks up glass immediately

reactions.reaction: drinks purposefully once conscious V1 engages

scenes.recognition_hook: Blindsight can dodge a chair or win a forced guess — ONLY conscious sight lets you look at a glass of water and choose to drink.
